key_insight: A spatial AI biomarker that detects high-risk morphology clusters at the invasive tumor front adds independent prognostic value beyond the overall slide score in early low- and intermediate-risk breast cancer.
clinical_relevance: This approach may better identify which patients with ER-positive/HER2-negative disease are truly low risk versus those who still need closer follow-up or additional treatment consideration.
method: 6106 Swedish breast cancer cases were split into a Stockholm training cohort and an independent Skåne test cohort.
A vision-transformer model (ViT_DG) scored tile-level high-grade morphology on whole-slide images.
A binary biomarker was defined by the presence of high-risk tile clusters at the invasive tumor front and tested with multivariable Cox models.
evidence_signal: In the ER-positive/HER2-negative/lymph-node-negative, grade 1-2 subgroup, cluster-positive status predicted worse recurrence outcomes, with an external test-set hazard ratio of 2.30 and retained value even among cases labeled low-risk by the global AI score.
watch_item: This is retrospective, pathology-image based evidence from a Swedish cohort, so external validation and workflow standardization are still needed before routine implementation.
paper_title: A spatial AI-based biomarker with independent prognostic value in early low- and intermediate- risk breast cancer
